task.title: Split status.go into per-verb files to match the priority layout
task.description:
Split internal/cli/status.go (2710 lines) and internal/cli/status_test.go (2562 lines) into per-verb files, matching the layout the workbook priority verbs use.

## Why

The priority verbs were built as one file per verb, because per-file ownership is what let several of them be written in parallel. Statuses are the same shape of command family living in one file too large to hold in your head, and the only reason for the difference is that statuses came first. After this, a reader who has found their way around one family has found their way around the other.

Also move regenerateGuidelines out of status.go into a neutral file. It regenerates the guidelines for status AND priority mutations, so living in status.go misnames it.

## The rule that matters: this is a pure move

No moved line may be edited. Not a rename, not a comment reflow, not a reordering of a function's contents, not a 'while I am here' fix. Go does not care which file in a package a declaration lives in, so a correct refactor changes nothing but file boundaries and import blocks. If something looks wrong while moving it, note it and move it unchanged, then fix it in its own change where a reviewer can see it.

Import blocks are the one permitted edit, because each new file needs its own and status.go sheds what it no longer uses. gofmt settles them.

## How to prove it was a pure move

Do not rely on 'I moved it carefully'.

Before touching anything, record the base commit, and capture a sorted list of every top-level declaration in status.go by grepping for lines beginning with func, type, var or const.

Move one file at a time, building after each rather than moving everything and then debugging.

Afterwards, regenerate that sorted declaration list across all the new status files and diff it against the before-picture. It must come back empty.

Then prove no body changed: for at least eight moved functions spanning every new file, extract each function as it was in the base commit and as it is in its new home, and diff the two. An empty diff per function is the evidence.

## Tests

Run the whole suite with a 45m timeout, not a slice of it. internal/cli takes about 12 minutes, and a refactor this size is exactly where a green slice and a red package diverge.

Split status_test.go the same way, each verb's tests beside its verb.

## Commit

One commit, so the move reverts as a unit and file history has a single hinge. Say in the message that no behavior changed, and how that was verified.

## For the reviewer

The interesting question is not 'does it build'. It is 'did anything change that was supposed to only move'. Check the declaration diff, spot-check function bodies against the base commit yourself rather than trusting the report, and confirm regenerateGuidelines did not gain or lose a caller in transit.

## Depends on

The workbook priority CLI verbs landing first, from the task 'Priorities should be configurable per project like Status'. The target layout has to exist and be proven before existing code is moved into it.
